sources.entry: SANE Network Scanning - Allow remote clients to access image acquisition devices (scanners) available on the local host. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C

summary.name: SANE
summary.one_liner: SANE (Scanner Access Now Easy) is an open source project providing a standard interface for accessing image acquisition devices such as flatbed scanners and cameras on Unix-like systems.
use_cases: share a scanner on a local host with remote clients
use a flatbed scanner on linux
scan documents from the command line
provide scanner access on a home server
build scanner frontends on top of a common backend
summary.what_it_does: The page is the SANE project start page. It lists the latest releases of sane-backends (1.4.0 released 2025-05-23, back to 1.0.31 in 2020) and a sane-frontends release (1.0.14, 2005). The listing describes SANE as a network scanning tool that lets remote clients access image acquisition devices (scanners) attached to the local host. Source code is hosted on GitLab and licensed GPL-2.0, with C as the main language. The page text itself contains little detail beyond release news and hosting information.
notable: Network scanning: remote clients can access scanners on the local host
Hosted on GitLab, GPL-2.0 licensed, written in C
Separate backends (drivers) and frontends (user programs) packages
caveats: Frontends package last released in 2005 according to the page
Page text gives little detail on supported devices or setup
